threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You keep ordering a flat white but still ask for sugar, while everyone else has already switched to oat milk and sea salt.
Saw a couple on the 68 bus passionately arguing over a half-eaten kebab. Can't blame them; those late-night snacks can stir up some real emotions.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a flock of pigeons chilling at the bus stop, waiting for the next BVG strike to end. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice Kreuzberg cafés serve a free slice of cake with your coffee if it’s your birthday? You’d think it’s a gimmick, but people actually celebrate there!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local will know to carry a sweater in July; those fogs hit without warning, while newcomers just sweat in the sun.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 47 bus serenading the driver with a ukulele. They both smiled like it was a regular Tuesday. Only in San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is just about Gaudí. They miss the real charm in our local tavernes and hidden plazas where the rhythms of daily life pulse.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still ask for a ‘café amb llet’ but never realize it's just ‘café con leche’ here. The locals just smile knowingly.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'Stokey' instead of Stoke Newington. Everyone here knows it's just Stokey, mate.
Last Saturday on the 59, a guy serenaded us with an old Beyoncé song. Must've rehearsed; he had all the moves, even spun the pole like a pro.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy in a full suit skateboarding past a protest while juggling three apples. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you catch a late-night U-Bahn with a DJ spinning in your car. It's like a secret rave on wheels.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they take the bus every day, ignoring the delays, while newcomers panic about BART's latest meltdown.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a suit singing to himself on the 22 Fillmore while a toddler directly across from him was silently staring, totally transfixed.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just walk into a plaça and find a quiet moment, but Gràcia's plazas are basically living rooms — bustling, noisy, and always full of locals.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they take photos of the street signs like they’re rare artifacts, oblivious to the locals rushing past.
